sample_unit: US adults with moderate-to-severe anxiety and depression symptoms (real-world study); 43,325 simulated responses in simulation

links.outcome: Harmful outputs in simulated high-risk synthetic patient conversations, including safety-critical scenarios
links.effect: Potentially harmful outputs occurred in <1 in 10,000 responses (0.01%, 95% CI [0.01%, 0.03%]) across 43,325 simulated responses; none encouraged harm to self or others.
links.quote: In simulation experiments, potentially harmful outputs occurred in <1 in 10,000 responses (0.01%, 95% CI [0.01%, 0.03%]); none encouraged harm to self or others, judged or actively invalidated the user, or used offensive language.

links.outcome: Offensive, invalidating or judgmental language in generative AI outputs during simulation
links.effect: No simulated outputs judged or actively invalidated the user or used offensive language.
links.quote: In simulation experiments, potentially harmful outputs occurred in <1 in 10,000 responses (0.01%, 95% CI [0.01%, 0.03%]); none encouraged harm to self or others, judged or actively invalidated the user, or used offensive language.

unlisted_practices: Constrained generative AI architecture (clinician-curated CBT content) for mental health agent
Multi-agent automated harm detection combined with clinician oversight
Large-scale synthetic patient simulation for safety testing

screen.reason: The study evaluates a multi-layered safety guardrail architecture (simulation testing, automated harm detection, and clinician oversight) for a generative AI mental health agent deployed to real patients.

primary.practice: multi-agent safety system combining automated harm detection and clinician oversight
